---
title: "Reconstruction"
---

Scores and loadings rebuild a matrix cell by cell. We evaluate that reconstruction with a matrix-completion task: learn segment structure from training inventories, choose rank with validation inventories, and reconstruct six cells hidden from each test inventory while its other retained segment cells remain visible.

## Reconstructing with the first $K$ terms

For centered training data,

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)}
=
\mathbf U_K\mathbf D_K\mathbf V_K^{\mathsf T}
=
\mathbf T_K\mathbf V_K^{\mathsf T}.
$$

The reconstructed centered cell is

$$
\widehat z_{ij}^{(K)}
=
\sum_{k=1}^{K}t_{ik}v_{jk}.
$$

Returning to the original listing scale adds the training column mean:

$$
\widehat x_{ij}^{(K)}
=
\widehat\mu_j
+
\widehat z_{ij}^{(K)}.
$$

For an observed training matrix, the residual is

$$
\mathbf E^{(K)}
=
\mathbf Z-\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(K)},
$$

and the fraction of centered sum of squares represented is

$$
R_K
=
\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{K}d_k^2}
     {\sum_{k=1}^{r}d_k^2}
=
1-
\frac{\|\mathbf E^{(K)}\|_F^2}
     {\|\mathbf Z\|_F^2}.
$$

This descriptive quantity assesses cells used in fitting. It is not held-out performance.

## Reconstructing partially observed inventories

Let $\mathbf x_i^*$ be a held-out inventory row in which hidden cells have been replaced by their training-column means. Their centered values are thus zero. For rank $K$,

$$
\widehat{\mathbf t}_i^{(K)}
=
(\mathbf x_i^*-\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu})^{\mathsf T}
\mathbf V_K,
$$

and

$$
\widehat{\mathbf x}_i^{(K)}
=
\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}
+
\mathbf V_K\widehat{\mathbf t}_i^{(K)}.
$$

This projection uses the observed cells to estimate a score. It is not a binary generative model, so fitted values may lie outside the unit interval. We clip them only when computing a probability loss.

## Building the split and masks

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

balanced_brier <- function(truth, prediction) {
  prediction <- pmin(pmax(prediction, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)
  loss <- (truth - prediction)^2
  listed <- as.logical(truth)
  mean(c(mean(loss[listed]), mean(loss[!listed])))
}

make_mask <- function(X, rows, seed, n_each = 3L) {
  set.seed(seed)
  mask <- matrix(FALSE, nrow = length(rows), ncol = ncol(X))
  for (i in seq_along(rows)) {
    listed <- which(X[rows[[i]], ] == 1)
    not_listed <- which(X[rows[[i]], ] == 0)
    mask[i, c(sample(listed, n_each), sample(not_listed, n_each))] <- TRUE
  }
  list(rows = rows, mask = mask)
}

reconstruct <- function(X, evaluation, mean, loadings, rank) {
  observed <- X[evaluation$rows, , drop = FALSE]
  mean_matrix <- matrix(rep(mean, each = nrow(observed)), nrow = nrow(observed))
  observed[evaluation$mask] <- mean_matrix[evaluation$mask]
  centered <- sweep(observed, 2, mean, "-")
  prediction <- mean_matrix
  if (rank > 0L) {
    directions <- loadings[, seq_len(rank), drop = FALSE]
    prediction <- prediction + centered %*% directions %*% t(directions)
  }
  pmin(pmax(prediction, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)
}

phoible <- readRDS("data/phoible/phoible-pilot.rds")
inventories <- phoible$inventories[
  order(phoible$inventories$glottocode,
        as.integer(phoible$inventories$inventory_id)),
]
groups <- split(seq_len(nrow(inventories)), inventories$glottocode)
RNGkind(sample.kind = "Rejection")
set.seed(20260827L)
chosen <- vapply(groups, function(x) x[[sample.int(length(x), 1L)]], integer(1))
selected <- inventories[unname(chosen), ]

area <- selected$macroarea
area[is.na(area) | area == ""] <- "Unclassified"
selected$split <- NA_character_
set.seed(20261018L)
for (name in sort(unique(area))) {
  index <- sample(which(area == name))
  n_holdout <- floor(0.15 * length(index))
  selected$split[index[seq_len(n_holdout)]] <- "validation"
  selected$split[index[n_holdout + seq_len(n_holdout)]] <- "test"
  selected$split[index[is.na(selected$split[index])]] <- "training"
}
training_rows <- which(selected$split == "training")
validation_rows <- which(selected$split == "validation")
test_rows <- which(selected$split == "test")

memberships <- merge(
  phoible$memberships,
  selected[c("inventory_id", "glottocode")],
  by = c("inventory_id", "glottocode")
)
frequency <- table(
  memberships$segment_id[memberships$glottocode %in%
    selected$glottocode[training_rows]]
)
column_ids <- sort(names(frequency)[frequency >= 20L])
X <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = nrow(selected),
  ncol = length(column_ids),
  dimnames = list(selected$glottocode, column_ids)
)
retained <- memberships[memberships$segment_id %in% column_ids, ]
X[cbind(
  match(retained$glottocode, rownames(X)),
  match(retained$segment_id, colnames(X))
)] <- 1

training_mean <- colMeans(X[training_rows, , drop = FALSE])
Z <- sweep(X[training_rows, , drop = FALSE], 2, training_mean, "-")
decomposition <- svd(Z, nu = 64L, nv = 64L)
validation <- make_mask(X, validation_rows, seed = 20261019L)
test <- make_mask(X, test_rows, seed = 20261020L)

candidate_ranks <- c(0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 5L, 8L, 12L, 16L,
                     24L, 32L, 40L, 50L, 64L) # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
validation_loss <- vapply(candidate_ranks, function(rank) {
  prediction <- reconstruct(X, validation, training_mean, decomposition$v, rank)
  truth <- X[validation$rows, , drop = FALSE][validation$mask]
  balanced_brier(truth, prediction[validation$mask])
}, numeric(1))
selected_rank <- candidate_ranks[[which.min(validation_loss)]]

test_prediction <- reconstruct(
  X, test, training_mean, decomposition$v, selected_rank
)
test_baseline <- reconstruct(X, test, training_mean, decomposition$v, 0L)
test_truth <- X[test$rows, , drop = FALSE][test$mask]

c(
  selected_rank = selected_rank,
  hidden_test_cells = sum(test$mask),
  baseline_balanced_brier =
    balanced_brier(test_truth, test_baseline[test$mask]),
  low_rank_balanced_brier =
    balanced_brier(test_truth, test_prediction[test$mask])
)
```

Validation selects rank `r selected_rank`. Only after that choice is fixed do we compute test loss. The segment-prevalence baseline has balanced Brier loss `r round(balanced_brier(test_truth, test_baseline[test$mask]), 4)`, whereas the low-rank reconstruction has loss `r round(balanced_brier(test_truth, test_prediction[test$mask]), 4)`.

## Showing raw hidden cells and predictions

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4

cells <- which(test$mask, arr.ind = TRUE)
prediction_data <- data.frame(
  status = factor(test_truth, levels = c(0, 1),
                  labels = c("Not listed", "Listed")),
  prediction = test_prediction[test$mask]
)

ggplot(prediction_data, aes(x = status, y = prediction)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.13, height = 0, color = "grey55",
              alpha = 0.24, size = 0.6) + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.34, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white",
               color = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.65) + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  labs(x = "Hidden database status", y = "Rank-selected prediction") +
  theme_classic()
```

The raw points show all `r sum(test$mask)` hidden test cells. The separated distributions indicate that the observed cells of a new inventory contain information about its hidden listings under this representation.

## Estimating the test gain

Balanced Brier loss gives listed and not-listed cells equal total weight:

$$
L_{\mathrm{bal}}
=
\frac{1}{2n_1}\sum_{x=1}(x-\widehat x)^2
+
\frac{1}{2n_0}\sum_{x=0}(x-\widehat x)^2.
$$

The following bootstrap resamples complete inventory records, preserving all six masked cells from a record.

```{r}
test_cells <- which(test$mask, arr.ind = TRUE)
cell_gain <- split(seq_along(test_truth), test_cells[, "row"])
gain_by_inventory <- vapply(cell_gain, function(index) {
  balanced_brier(test_truth[index], test_baseline[test$mask][index]) -
    balanced_brier(test_truth[index], test_prediction[test$mask][index])
}, numeric(1))

set.seed(20261021L)
bootstrap_gain <- replicate(5000L, mean(sample(gain_by_inventory, replace = TRUE)))
gain_interval <- quantile(bootstrap_gain, c(0.025, 0.975))
c(
  mean_gain = mean(gain_by_inventory),
  interval_low = gain_interval[[1]],
  interval_high = gain_interval[[2]]
)
```

The test loss gain is `r round(mean(gain_by_inventory), 4)`, with an inventory bootstrap interval from `r round(gain_interval[[1]], 4)` to `r round(gain_interval[[2]], 4)`. This interval describes inventory-record variability under the present split. It is not a family-level typological interval.

## What reconstruction establishes

The result supports a narrow conclusion: structure learned from training inventory records helps complete a few hidden database listings when most of a held-out record is observed. It does not reconstruct a wholly unseen inventory, establish phonological absence from a zero, or show that rank `r selected_rank` is a phonological universal.

## Checking the rebuilt cells

1. Why are hidden cells filled with training-column means before projection?
2. Which cells estimate a held-out inventory's scores?
3. Why is observed reconstruction error not held-out prediction error?
4. Why does balanced Brier loss weight the two cell statuses equally?
5. What is the unit resampled by the bootstrap?

The [next page](choosing-components.qmd) isolates the validation step that selected the retained rank without inspecting test loss.
